column1: # Phiogy's mark, drawn on the measures of the face Phiogy is set in:
# name, how many, and of which measure of the font. The measures are
# read from the font file by script/logo.py: `stem` (an upright stroke),
# `thin` (a lying one, the hyphen's height), `round` (how wide the o
# is), `drop` (how far the p goes under the line), `one` (1). Nothing
# here is a size by eye. The mark is the web Phiogy's (puikit:
# app/phiogy/mark.py): the letter o, a voice, with a tail that makes a
# speech mark of it.
font
# How much of the picture is left clear round the mark.
room
# The tail: as thick as a stem, it leaves the o's foot half a stem in
# from its left side, drops half as far as the p goes under the line,
# and leans out by half a stem as it drops. Its ends are round.
tail.thick
tail.inset
tail.lean
tail.drop
# Which mark is written into asset/icon: `voice` (the o with a tail),
# or `p` and an option of data/logo-corner.tsv. Every drawing is kept
# in doc/logo/ whichever is chosen. `drawn` is the user's choice (22
# November 2026, "use this and we're done"): the picture as it was
# given.
mark
# `tall` is how high the o is.
# The p with two bars cut out of it, as the picture the user gave on 22
# November 2026 has it; each number is that picture's own proportion,
# said in the font's measures and checked by laying the drawing over
# the picture: 74 of its 5,695 dots differ. Its bowl is as high as the
# o and a little wider, filled; its top right corner is rounder than
# its bottom right one.
p.wide
p.high
p.corner
p.corner.low
# Its two left corners are round too: the top left, and the stem's
# foot at the left (the heel). The picture's own file cuts them square;
# the user saw it in the conversation with its corners round, chose
# that look (22 November 2026: "you rounded the bottom left corner",
# "that's what we want") and gave a screenshot of it to lay the drawing
# over. Both numbers are fitted to that screenshot: 63 of its dots
# differ, all single dots at the edges. The heel is rounder than the
# stem is long, so its curve begins a little over the bowl's foot.
p.left
p.heel
# The stem under the bowl at the left: half as wide again as a stem.
# Where it meets the bowl's foot is a round hollow, and the mark ends
# where that curve ends, as the picture does: the stem's foot is sharp
# at the right, where the hollow's curve comes down to it, which makes
# a point of it as a bird's tail is. A longer stem or a foot round at
# the right is not the picture's.
p.tail.wide
p.tail.drop
p.hollow
p.foot
# The long bar: a wall in from the left, under the top, how wide and
# how high, and how round a round corner of it is.
p.wall
p.top
p.bar.wide
p.bar.high
p.bar.corner
# The short bar beside it: how far apart, how wide, where it starts
# under the bowl's top, how high; its round corners are half its width.
p.gap
# Two thirds as wide as the long bar (0.88 of a stem): the user's word
# on 23 November 2026. The picture's own was 0.58.
p.dot.wide
p.dot.top
# Half as high as the long bar (2 to 1), so that the two are seen to
# differ: the user's word on 23 November 2026, after two thirds (3 to
# 2) had been tried that day. The picture's own was 0.418 of the o's
# height. It keeps its top.
p.dot.high
p.dot.corner
# In the mark's file a round corner is a true curve. Where the mark is
# drawn as dots (the sheet of options), it is a point every so many
# degrees.
p.fine
# The sheet of options (doc/logo-option.png): the sides each option is
# shown at, the first large and the others the bar's sizes; the room
# between things; how much of a square is clear round the mark; how
# many times as large it is drawn before it is brought down; the
# sheet's own ground, ink and size of text.
sheet.side
sheet.gap
sheet.room
sheet.fine
sheet.paper
sheet.ink
sheet.text
# The inks the mark is tried in, each as ink and ground. A token is the
# theme's colour; after `dark/` the dark look's. The blue is a stand-in:
# no blue is named anywhere in the kit, so any other replaces it here.
try.black
try.white
try.blue
try.blue on dark
try.white on blue
# The mark as the web's kit keeps one (doc/logo/registry-icon.json): a
# square box that wide, the mark that high in its middle.
web.box
web.high
